source_text: Et ne locus quidem eis erat in diversorio. Locum non habuit, qui caelum et terram verbo extruxit. Quoniam cum dives esset, propter nos factus est pauper, extremam vilitatem ob salutem naturae nostrae eligens, ex ingenita sua in nos bonitate.
orientation: The homilist continues the birth narrative after the laying of the child in the manger.
pass_a_gloss: And not even a place was for them in the inn. He had no place, who built heaven and earth by his word. Since although he was rich, on account of us he was made poor, choosing extreme lowliness on account of the salvation of our nature, out of his inborn goodness toward us.

choices.why: ne...quidem with negation stresses not even so much as a place
concrete lodging-place for travelers, matching Luke 2:7 context
extruo means build up erect, verb preserves creation by word
vilitas is low worth or meanness, not moral vileness here

bible_refs.note: quia non erat eis locus in diversorio
cum dives esset, propter nos factus est pauper

pass_b_english: And there was not even a place for them in the inn (Luke 2:7). He who built heaven and earth by his word had no place. For though he was rich, he became poor for our sake (2 Corinthians 8:9). He chose extreme lowliness for the salvation of our nature, out of his innate goodness toward us.
